A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CogVideoX. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, and retained material can be matched despite substantial renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original automated and human evaluations in Tables 1–2, training-loss ablations in Figure 4, and generated examples in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical evaluations and adds VAE comparisons, architecture and attention experiments, and held-out data-filter results.

M1.justification: The stated VAE reconstruction loss changes from L2 to L1. Section 2.2 replaces explicitly spatial-only patching with a formulation permitting temporal patches and first-frame repetition. Section 3.1 extends Frame Pack to mixed resolutions. These revise substantive procedures while retaining the central VAE, Expert AdaLN, and full-attention architecture.

E1.justification: v2 newly uses WebVid for ablation and reconstruction evaluation, extending evaluated data coverage within the existing video domain. Text-to-video, image-to-video, and video-to-video generation already appear in v1. Naming LAION-5B and COYO-700M provides training-source information but does not itself establish new domain coverage, since v1 already trains jointly on images and videos.

E2.justification: The main generation comparators and Kling remain unchanged. New comparisons evaluate SDXL's 2D VAE, Open-Sora and Open-Sora-Plan VAEs, MMDiT variants, and a model without Expert AdaLN. The previous learnable-position and Expert AdaLN-plus-MLP comparisons are removed from the revised ablations.

E3.justification: v2 introduces FVD evaluation on 500 WebVid videos, VAE reconstruction testing on 256×256, 17-frame videos, and filter evaluation using a 10% test subset. MMDiT controls match either parameter count or layer count. Training is described with four stages in Table 5 rather than v1's three-stage outline; the PDFs do not establish that retained benchmark results were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds compression/channel ablations, architecture and separated-attention tests, FVD evidence for uniform sampling, and filter validation. The learnable-position and additional-expert-MLP ablations disappear. The RoPE-versus-sinusoidal and sampling loss curves remain, while the interpolation/extrapolation example moves to Appendix A. Appendix G also adds a captioning case study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added evaluations continue to report point results and training trajectories without identified uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial VAE, FVD, and filter results. Table 2 reports flickering/PSNR of 85.5/29.1 for its VAE, versus 92.4/28.5 for Open-Sora and 90.2/27.6 for Open-Sora-Plan; Table 11 reports filter accuracies of 0.89–0.99. All main generation and human-evaluation scores remain unchanged. The prose now attributes five metric wins specifically to 5B, although Table 3 gives it four outright maxima; the fifth belongs to 2B.

T1.justification: Section 2.2 revises the token-count expression from T(H/p)(W/p) to (T/q)(H/p)(W/p), introducing temporal patch size q. This is a limited mathematical specification change. The diffusion objective in Equation 1 remains unchanged, and no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: v1 describes the released model as generating 720×480, six-second videos at eight fps. v2 claims generation up to 768×1360, ten seconds, and 16 fps across multiple aspect ratios without super-resolution or frame interpolation. Its introduction also expands the release contribution to both 2B and 5B text-to-video and image-to-video models and introduces a commercial-grade priority claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds discussion of convergence difficulties under aggressive VAE compression, explains resolution generalization through the absence of attention modules, and acknowledges that competing VAEs use fewer latent channels. It also positions Expert AdaLN's simplicity as advantageous for scaling. The earlier warning that high-quality fine-tuning slightly harms semantic ability remains in Appendix A.

D1.justification: Tables 5–6 newly disclose training budgets, batch sizes, model dimensions, optimizer settings, and precision. v2 also specifies VAE frame counts, resolution, GAN warm-up, image sources, and caption-model access. Some settings remain unreconciled, including 512-pixel training in Section 3.2 versus 480 pixels in Table 5. The earlier human-evaluation blinding/randomization statement is omitted, without establishing that the procedure changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for SDXL, CogVLM2, LAION-5B, and COYO-700M and explicitly positions Expert AdaLN against MMDiT. Several baseline and long-context references are removed, even though the corresponding generation baselines remain evaluated. The new commercial-grade priority claim also adjusts novelty positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, conclusion, and several methodological and evaluation passages are substantially rewritten. v2 adds a contribution list and dedicated ablation subsection, introduces an appendix contents list, and reorganizes training details and loss curves into Appendices A–B. Earlier Appendices A–F become D–I, with additional material moved from the main text.

P2.justification: v2 adds an opening showcase, VAE and training tables, FVD plots, and caption/filter illustrations; redraws Frame Pack; and replaces two panels in the relocated loss-curve figure. Typography, figure wrapping, and table placement change throughout. Many existing showcases are retained. The new Figure 8 incorrectly swaps the FVD and training-step axis labels.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for central design choices that v1 supported mainly through explanation and limited loss ablations. Reconstruction benchmarks, architecture controls, attention tests, and detailed training specifications improve validation and reproducibility without changing the headline benchmark scores. These gains outweigh the removed smaller ablations and reporting defects, including swapped FVD axes, unreconciled settings, and the overstated attribution of five metric wins to 5B.
